I want to talk about the importance of personal creativity and how it directly shapes our well-being and sense of fulfillment.

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Grief is a private experience, yet it reshapes every part of our public lives. After the sudden loss of my 17-year-old son, I found myself lost in silence trying to function in a world that no longer made sense. As a mother, I was devastated. As an educator, I was expected to keep showing up. 
 
 In the few weeks that followed, I paused to reflect on my son’s life, his discipline, his goals, and the stories his friends shared about how he inspired them. I realized he had already become the kind of role model many people spend decades trying to be. His legacy wasn’t only in what he planned to do, it was in how he lived, and how he made others feel seen. That gave me perspective. I wanted to follow his lead.
 
 I chose to carry his light forward.
 
 This talk is about how purpose can emerge through pain, and how vulnerability, when embraced and not hidden, can lead to connection, healing, and meaning. I didn’t overcome grief. I live with it. But I also found purpose in service to others

author: TEDx Talks
description:
We often think of boredom as an annoying, useless feeling in life amidst the screens, noise, and constant stimulation. But neuroscience reveals something different: boredom is not a glitch in the brain, but rather, a signal. A signal that most of us are ignoring. 
 
Boredom happens when the brain's reward system expects something, but nothing happens. When dopamine dips, the brain shifts into a unique state where two networks are activated: the default mode, which is responsible for daydreaming and creative insight, and the salience network, which pushes us to seek something new. Together, they create a tension with one part of the brain drifting and other searching. 
 
 This combination is rare and creates an important stage for identity shifts and life decisions. Studies show that boredom actually increases creativity and improves problem-solving, alongside motivating people to pursue their goals. In essence, boredom is not the absence of meaning, but the brain demanding more of it.
title: When Nothing Happens, Everything Starts | Alekhya Buragadda | TEDxBGSU
